title: What to Bring to the Florida Real Estate Exam
metaDesc: Two forms of signature ID, your Pearson VUE confirmation, and your pre-license certificate. What's required, what's allowed, and what to leave at home.
h1: What to Bring to the Florida Real Estate Exam
about: What to bring, and what not to bring, to the Florida real estate sales associate exam at a Pearson VUE test center

hub.name: Become a Real Estate Agent in Florida

answer: Bring two forms of valid signature identification (one must be government-issued, like a driver's license or passport), your Pearson VUE booking confirmation, and your pre-license course completion certificate. A basic handheld calculator is allowed at test centers. Leave notes, phones, bags, and study materials at home or in your car, since none of it is allowed in the testing room. Plan to arrive about 30 minutes before your scheduled time.
takeaways: Two forms of signature ID are required, and at least one has to be government-issued (driver's license, state ID, passport, or military ID).
Bring your printed or digital Pearson VUE booking confirmation and your pre-license course completion certificate.
A basic handheld calculator is allowed for the math portion at in-person test centers.
Phones, notes, study materials, and bags aren't permitted in the testing room. Leave them in your car.
Arrive about 30 minutes early. Test centers don't guarantee a late arrival will still be seated.
tldr: For the Florida real estate exam at a Pearson VUE test center, bring two forms of signature ID (one government-issued), your booking confirmation, your pre-license course completion certificate, and a basic calculator. Leave your phone, notes, and any study materials outside the testing room, and arrive about 30 minutes early.

howto.name: Confirm your two forms of ID
howto.text: Bring two forms of valid signature identification. At least one must be government-issued, such as a driver's license, state ID card, passport, or military ID. Make sure the name matches exactly what you used to register.

howto.name: Bring your Pearson VUE booking confirmation
howto.text: Print or save a copy of your exam appointment confirmation from Pearson VUE, and bring it with you to the test center.

howto.name: Bring your pre-license course completion certificate
howto.text: Have your 63-hour pre-license course completion certificate, or accepted equivalent, ready to present.

howto.name: Pack a basic handheld calculator
howto.text: A basic, non-programmable calculator is allowed at in-person test centers for the math questions. Leave anything with text storage or internet capability at home.

howto.name: Leave prohibited items in your car
howto.text: Notes, reference materials, phones, other electronic devices, purses, briefcases, backpacks, and study books aren't allowed in the testing room. Plan to leave them locked in your car, not carry them in.

howto.name: Arrive about 30 minutes early
howto.text: Give yourself time to check in, store any items you weren't supposed to bring inside, and settle in before your scheduled start time.

body:
What identification do you need for the Florida real estate exam?

You need two forms of valid signature identification, and at least one of them has to be government-issued: a driver's license, state ID card, passport, or military ID both work. Make sure the name on your ID matches exactly what you used when you registered for the exam, since a mismatch can cause a problem at check-in.

What paperwork should you bring?

Bring your Pearson VUE booking confirmation, printed or saved on your phone before you leave (since your phone itself won't be allowed inside), along with your pre-license course completion certificate. Test centers check both before you're seated, so having them ready saves time at check-in.

Can you bring a calculator?

Yes, a basic handheld calculator is allowed at in-person test centers for the math portion of the exam. It needs to be a simple, non-programmable model, not anything with text storage, a QWERTY keyboard, or internet capability. If you're not sure whether yours qualifies, bring the simplest one you own.

What's not allowed in the testing room?

Notes, reference materials, textbooks, phones, smartwatches, and bags of any kind (purses, briefcases, backpacks) all stay outside the testing room. Most centers provide a secure area or lockers for personal items, but the safest approach is leaving anything you don't need locked in your car.

How early should you arrive?

Plan to arrive about 30 minutes before your scheduled appointment. This gives you time to check in, verify your ID, and get settled before the exam starts. Arriving late can mean losing your appointment entirely, since test centers run on a tight schedule for every candidate that day.

After you pass

Once you've passed, the next step is activating your license under a sponsoring broker. If you're deciding where to start that next chapter, a non-competing Adams, Cameron & Co. manager, part of the largest brokerage in Volusia and Flagler counties since 1963, will walk you through it. Start a confidential conversation.

Exam-day requirements are set by Pearson VUE and the DBPR and can change. Confirm current requirements directly before your appointment. Educational only, not legal advice.

faq.q: What ID do you need for the Florida real estate exam?
faq.a: Two forms of valid signature identification, with at least one being government-issued, such as a driver's license, state ID, passport, or military ID. The name must match your exam registration exactly.

faq.q: Can you bring a calculator to the Florida real estate exam?
faq.a: Yes, a basic, non-programmable handheld calculator is allowed at in-person Pearson VUE test centers for the math questions.

faq.q: Can you bring your phone into the testing room?
faq.a: No. Phones, along with notes, study materials, and bags, aren't permitted in the testing room and typically need to stay in your car or a designated storage area.

faq.q: What paperwork do you need at the Florida real estate exam?
faq.a: Your Pearson VUE booking confirmation and your pre-license course completion certificate, in addition to your two forms of ID.

faq.q: How early should you arrive for the exam?
faq.a: About 30 minutes before your scheduled appointment time, to allow for check-in and ID verification.
